pois.name: Ponte di Tiberio
pois.blurb: The Ponte di Tiberio is a Roman bridge in Rimini, Italy. Begun under Augustus and completed under Tiberius in 21 AD, it remains a usable crossing for pedestrians.

themeConnection.text: Roman stone bridge over the Marecchia, completed in the early first century and still walkable.

pois.name: Puente Romano
pois.blurb: The Puente Romano is an ancient Roman bridge over the Guadiana River at Mérida. Much of its historic masonry survives, and the bridge is accessible for pedestrians.

themeConnection.text: Long surviving Roman bridge over the Guadiana, preserved as a pedestrian crossing within Mérida.

pois.name: Ponte Sant'Angelo
pois.blurb: Ponte Sant'Angelo, originally the Aelian Bridge or Pons Aelius, is a Roman bridge in Rome, Italy, completed in 134 AD by Roman Emperor Hadrian (Publius Aelius Hadrianus), to span the Tiber from the city centre to his newly constructed mausoleum, now the towering Castel…

themeConnection.text: Ancient Roman bridge substantially retaining historic fabric and now used as a pedestrian crossing to Castel Sant'Angelo.

pois.name: Stone Bridge
pois.blurb: The Stone Bridge is a medieval bridge in Regensburg, Germany, crossing the Danube. Constructed between 1135 and 1146, it is a historic public crossing now used primarily by pedestrians.

themeConnection.text: Twelfth-century stone bridge over the Danube, a preserved historic pedestrian crossing in central Regensburg.

pois.name: Ponte Vecchio
pois.blurb: The Ponte Vecchio is a medieval stone closed-spandrel segmental arch bridge over the Arno River in Florence. It is known for shops built along it and remains a pedestrian route.

themeConnection.text: Medieval enclosed stone bridge over the Arno, carrying a public pedestrian street and shops.

pois.name: Brooklyn Bridge
pois.blurb: The Brooklyn Bridge is a cable-stayed suspension bridge in New York City, spanning the East River between the boroughs of Manhattan and Brooklyn.

themeConnection.text: Nineteenth-century suspension bridge over the East River with a dedicated public pedestrian promenade.

pois.name: Rialto Bridge
pois.blurb: The Rialto Bridge is the oldest of the four bridges spanning the Grand Canal in Venice. The present stone bridge was completed in 1591 and includes pedestrian arcades and shops.

themeConnection.text: Late-sixteenth-century stone bridge across the Grand Canal with public pedestrian passage through its arcades.

pois.name: Charles Bridge
pois.blurb: Charles Bridge is a historic bridge that crosses the Vltava river in Prague, Czech Republic. Construction began in 1357 and the bridge has long served pedestrian movement across the river.

themeConnection.text: Medieval stone pedestrian bridge across the Vltava, completed in the 15th century and still open to ordinary pedestrians.

pois.name: Stone Bridge
pois.blurb: The Stone Bridge is a historic bridge across the Vardar River in Skopje. Built during the Ottoman period in the fifteenth century, it remains a public pedestrian route.

themeConnection.text: Fifteenth-century Ottoman stone bridge across the Vardar, preserved as a pedestrian crossing.

pois.name: Ponte delle Torri
pois.blurb: The Ponte delle Torri is a medieval bridge and aqueduct spanning the deep ravine below Spoleto. Its elevated walkway and historic structure form a publicly accessible pedestrian route.

themeConnection.text: Medieval aqueduct-bridge across a ravine, now used as a public pedestrian route within Spoleto.

pois.name: Puente Romano
pois.blurb: The Roman bridge of Córdoba crosses the Guadalquivir in the historic center of Córdoba. Its origins are Roman, and the bridge is now closed to motor traffic and open to pedestrians.

themeConnection.text: Ancient Roman bridge across the Guadalquivir, now pedestrian-only and retaining historic piers and structure.

pois.name: Roman Bridge of Aosta
pois.blurb: The Roman Bridge of Aosta is an ancient stone bridge in the Italian city of Aosta. Built during the Roman period over the Buthier, it remains a visible and accessible crossing.

themeConnection.text: First-century Roman masonry bridge over the Buthier, retained within the city and walkable by pedestrians.

pois.name: Ponte Pietra
pois.blurb: Ponte Pietra is a Roman arch bridge crossing the Adige River in Verona. Although repaired many times, it retains ancient and medieval elements and is open to pedestrians.

themeConnection.text: Ancient and medieval stone bridge across the Adige, open to pedestrian crossing and retaining substantial historic fabric.

pois.name: Puente de Besalú
pois.blurb: The bridge of Besalú is a medieval fortified bridge crossing the Fluvià River in the town of Besalú. Its stone arches and gate tower form a walkable public route.

themeConnection.text: Medieval fortified bridge across the Fluvià, preserved at its historic site and open to pedestrians.

pois.name: Pulteney Bridge
pois.blurb: Pulteney Bridge is a bridge over the River Avon in Bath, England. It was completed by 1774, and connected the city with land in Bathwick which Sir William Pulteney and his family wished to develop.

themeConnection.text: Eighteenth-century bridge over the River Avon with shops and an ordinary public pedestrian crossing.

pois.name: Triple Bridge
pois.blurb: Triple Bridge is a group of three bridges across the Ljubljanica in Ljubljana. The central bridge dates from 1842, while the side pedestrian bridges were added later to form the walkable complex.

themeConnection.text: Historic central bridge complex whose original stone bridge dates to the nineteenth century and is pedestrian-accessible.

pois.name: Krämerbrücke
pois.blurb: The Krämerbrücke (pronounced [ˈkʁɛːmɐˌbʁʏkə]; Merchants' bridge) is a medieval arch bridge in the city of Erfurt, in Thuringia, central Germany, which is lined with half-timbered shops and houses on both sides of a cobblestone street.

themeConnection.text: Medieval inhabited bridge across the Breitstrom, still functioning as a public pedestrian street.

pois.name: Puente de Piedra
pois.blurb: The Puente de Piedra (English: Stone Bridge) is a bridge across the river Ebro in Zaragoza, Spain. The Puente de Piedra is also called the Bridge of Lions because since 1991 four lions (symbols of the city) have been placed on the pillars at each end of the bridge.

themeConnection.text: Fifteenth-century stone bridge over the Ebro with current pedestrian access and historic fabric.

pois.name: Eads Bridge
pois.blurb: Eads Bridge is a historic steel arch bridge across the Mississippi River at St. Louis. Completed in 1874, it has a pedestrian walkway and remains an important public crossing.

themeConnection.text: Nineteenth-century steel arch bridge over the Mississippi with a public pedestrian and cycling walkway.

pois.name: Old Bridge
pois.blurb: Heidelberg's Old Bridge is a historic stone bridge over the Neckar. The present bridge was built in 1788 and includes preserved medieval gate towers; pedestrians routinely cross it.

themeConnection.text: Eighteenth-century stone bridge over the Neckar, open to pedestrians and retaining historic towers and masonry.

clue.text: An ancient Roman crossing faced in travertine marble spans a major river with five arches; it is now solely pedestrian and leads directly toward a historic mausoleum transformed into a castle.

theme.title: Historic Walkable Bridges in Cities
theme.introduction: Old spans carry footsteps over rivers, linking city streets to centuries of travel.
theme.inclusionCriteria: Include only a location satisfying every condition: (1) it is an individually named bridge or bridge complex whose established function is carrying people across water, a ravine, or another physical obstacle; (2) the present bridge retains substantial historic fabric and was opened, completed, or substantially rebuilt at its current site on or before 31 December 1899; (3) ordinary pedestrians can currently cross or walk onto it during normal public access, whether freely or by admission; (4) it lies within the current administrative boundary of a present-day city or incorporated urban municipality; (5) the bridge itself, rather than merely a viewpoint or surrounding district, can be pinned as one exact map location. Plausible locations include Charles Bridge (Prague), Rialto Bridge (Venice), Ponte Vecchio (Florence), Ponte Sant’Angelo (Rome), Ponte Sisto (Rome), Ponte Pietra (Verona), Ponte Scaligero (Verona), Ponte di Tiberio (Rimini), Ponte Coperto (Pavia), Pont Neuf (Paris), Pont Marie (Paris), Pont de la Tournelle (Paris), Pont Saint-Bénézet (Avignon), Pont Vieux (Albi), Pont Valentré (Cahors), Stari Most (Mostar), Krämerbrücke (Erfurt), Pulteney Bridge (Bath), Old Bridge (Heidelberg), Stone Bridge (Regensburg), Clifton Suspension Bridge (Bristol), Bridge of Sighs (Cambridge), Mathematical Bridge (Cambridge), Brooklyn Bridge (New York City), Eads Bridge (St. Louis), Széchenyi Chain Bridge (Budapest), Liberty Bridge (Budapest), Margaret Bridge (Budapest), Triple Bridge (Ljubljana), Stone Bridge (Skopje), Kintai Bridge (Iwakuni), Puente Romano (Córdoba), Puente Romano (Mérida), Puente de Piedra (Zaragoza), Puente de San Martín (Toledo), Puente de Alcántara (Toledo), Puente Nuevo (Ronda), Puente de Besalú, and Puente de la Reina Victoria (Madrid).
